I can't rule out up, right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going down would strand cell (1,6): it would be left with only one free neighbour. So my guess (right from number 2) was wrong, so the line must go down.
The line must go right: down is number 8, which comes later.
Going left would force the line onto number 5 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,2). So the line goes down.
Going right would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (6 cells); going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes up.
Going left would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (3,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
